conventions: stop entries mechanized as signal-bar-close then next-bar-open; every tunable constant is a parameter; long side only in pseudocode; helpers: highest(x,n)/lowest(x,n) over bars 0..n-1, ema(close,n), atr(n), swingHigh(k)/swingLow(k) = k-th most recent confirmed pivot, trendLine(...)/channelLine(...) = projected line value at bar 0. candidates.quote: Usually the first breakout of a tight, prolonged channel will fail. The trend will then resume and often break out to a new extreme
candidates.description: Filter: block countertrend entries on the first breakout against a tight channel (T15-10 true for at least minChannelBars). Count breakouts (bars closing beyond the channel's trend line) since the tight channel started; allow the fade only when breakoutCount >= 2 or a breakout pullback has formed (T15-38).
candidates.pseudocode: tightChannelAge >= minChannelBars && breakoutCountSinceChannelStart >= 2
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (filter)

complexity.reason: persisted channel age and breakout counter tied to a projected line

notes: p265: when the first breakout fails the resumed trend often reaches a measured move equal to the height of that failed reversal attempt (a further Exit target).

candidates.name: TrendBarCountInWindow
candidates.quote: maybe there were two or three good-sized bull trend bars within the past several bars
candidates.description: Reversal-strength filter: at least minCount bull trend bars (body >= bodyFraction of range, range >= largeBarAtrMultiple x ATR) among the last windowBars.
candidates.pseudocode: count over i in 0..windowBars-1 of (close[i] > open[i] && (close[i] - open[i]) >= bodyFraction * (high[i] - low[i]) && (high[i] - low[i]) >= largeBarAtrMultiple * atr(atrLength)) >= minCount
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (context)

complexity.reason: window count with ATR

candidates.name: BreakoutPullbackEntry
candidates.quote: Instead, it is better to wait to see if there is a breakout pullback, which can be a lower low or a higher low. If there is and the reversal up looks strong ... then you can consider buying the breakout pullback.
candidates.description: After an upside breakout (close above the prior swing high / bear trend line within the last maxBarsSinceBreakout), the market pulls back for at least one bar (low below prior low) and then a bar closes above the prior bar's high; buy at the next open. The pullback may make a higher low or a lower low.
candidates.pseudocode: breakoutBar within last maxBarsSinceBreakout with close > highest(high, breakoutLookback) at that time; since then exists a pullback bar with low < prior low; close[0] > high[1]
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the pullback's bull signal bar

complexity.reason: multi-stage state (breakout, pullback, resumption) that must persist across bars

notes: p259: if the reversal attempt after a breakout is weak, it sets up a breakout pullback within a bar or two (T15-43).

candidates.name: FirstPullbackAboveMovingAverage
candidates.quote: The odds of the long being profitable are better if the rally up goes above the moving average and that first pullback stays above the moving average.
candidates.description: Strength filter for a breakout pullback long: the rally crossed above the EMA and the pullback's lowest low (over the last pullbackBars) is still above the EMA.
candidates.pseudocode: close[0] > ma && lowest(low, pullbackBars) > ma
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (filter)

complexity.reason: EMA plus a small window

notes: Negation: if the first pullback forms below the EMA the bulls are weaker and a second leg is less likely.

candidates.name: FirstPullbackWithinNBarsAfterBreakout
candidates.quote: If there is no pullback and the market races upward, then the odds of even higher prices are good and you can wait for any pullback, which should come within five bars or so.
candidates.description: After a breakout bar (close above the highest high of breakoutLookback) with at least raceBars further bars making higher highs, buy the first bar whose low is below the prior bar's low, provided it arrives within maxWaitBars of the breakout.
candidates.pseudocode: barsSince(breakoutBar) <= maxWaitBars && consecutive higher highs since breakout >= raceBars && low[0] < low[1]
candidates.book_order_type: limit / buy above the pullback bar

complexity.reason: bars-since-breakout counter

candidates.name: LowBarOverlapWindow
candidates.quote: If the rally is in a very tight, steep channel with no pullbacks and very little overlap between the bars, and the rally goes far above the bull high before having any pause or pullback, the momentum is strong
candidates.description: Momentum filter: the average overlap between consecutive bars over the last windowBars, as a fraction of the prior bar's range, is at most maxOverlap. Low overlap = strong momentum; its negation (many overlapping bars) flags a weak test likely to form a lower high (p259).
candidates.pseudocode: overlap(i) = max(0, min(high[i], high[i+1]) - max(low[i], low[i+1])) / (high[i+1] - low[i+1]); average over i in 0..windowBars-1 of overlap(i) <= maxOverlap
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (context)

complexity.reason: window average of a two-bar quantity

notes: p270: 10 bear trend bars with little overlap and large bodies with small tails were climactic; combine with T15-52 for the climax reading.

candidates.name: ReversalBarStrongerThanBreakoutBar
candidates.quote: If the reversal bar is strong compared to the breakout bar, the odds of a failed breakout and a successful reversal are good.
candidates.description: Failed-breakout fade. Long side: bar[1] is a bear breakout bar (bear trend bar closing below the lowest low of breakoutLookback) and bar[0] is a bull reversal bar whose body is at least strengthRatio x the breakout bar's body; buy at the next open.
candidates.pseudocode: close[1] < open[1] && close[1] < lowest(low, breakoutLookback) shifted to bar 2 && close[0] > open[0] && (close[0] - open[0]) >= strengthRatio * (open[1] - close[1])
candidates.book_order_type: stop one tick above the reversal bar

complexity.reason: two adjacent bars plus a lowest-low window

notes: Negation: a reversal bar weaker than the breakout bar predicts a breakout pullback and resumption.

candidates.name: ThirdBarConfirmsFailedBreakout
candidates.quote: If it trades below the bear reversal bar, the breakout has failed, at least for the moment. If it then has a strong bear close and is a strong bear trend bar, the chance that the reversal will continue down increases.
candidates.description: When breakout bar and reversal bar are about equally strong, wait for the third bar. Long side: bar[2] bear breakout bar, bar[1] bull reversal bar of comparable body, bar[0] trades above bar[1]'s high and closes as a bull trend bar; buy at the next open.
candidates.pseudocode: close[2] < open[2] && close[1] > open[1] && abs((close[1]-open[1]) - (open[2]-close[2])) <= equalTol * (open[2]-close[2]) && high[0] > high[1] && close[0] > open[0] && (close[0]-open[0]) >= bodyFraction * (high[0]-low[0])
candidates.book_order_type: already entered on the stop above the reversal bar; the third bar decides whether to hold

complexity.reason: three fixed-offset bars

candidates.name: ThirdBarBreakoutPullbackReentry
candidates.quote: If instead it is a strong bull reversal bar, chances are that the failed breakout will not succeed, and this bull reversal bar then becomes a signal bar for a breakout pullback buy at one tick above its high.
candidates.description: With-trend re-entry after a reversal attempt fails. Long side: bar[3] bull breakout bar, bar[2] bear reversal bar, bar[1] a bull reversal bar (the reversal attempt failed), bar[0] closes above bar[1]'s high; buy at the next open.
candidates.pseudocode: close[3] > open[3] && close[3] > highest(high, breakoutLookback) at bar 4 && close[2] < open[2] && close[1] > open[1] && close[0] > high[1]
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the bull reversal bar

complexity.reason: fixed offsets plus a highest-high window

candidates.name: CorrectionToChannelStartTarget
candidates.quote: That pullback often has to go all the way to the beginning of the channel, where they began buying earlier, and this is part of the reason why channels often lead to a correction all the way to the bottom of the channel, where there is usually a bounce.
candidates.description: Target for a short taken at the end of a bull channel: exit when price reaches the channel's starting low (the first swing low of the channel). Long side (short-covering mirror written as a long taken at the end of a bear channel): exit when high[0] >= the swing high where the bear channel began.
candidates.pseudocode: ctx.MarketPosition() > 0 && high[0] >= channelStartPrice - tolAtr * atr(atrLength)
candidates.book_order_type: limit order near the start of the channel

complexity.reason: needs the channel's first pivot persisted

notes: p254: the bounce at the channel start is often followed by a trading range.

candidates.name: FadeTrendBarCloseBeyondSwingHigh
candidates.quote: Bears will short the closes of bull trend bars above prior swing highs, like the bar after bar 22, and the closes of small bull bars that follow, like bar 23, for scalps.
candidates.description: Countertrend scalp in a two-sided channel. Long side: a bear trend bar closes below the lowest low of the prior lookback bars (excluding the current bar); buy at the next open.
candidates.pseudocode: close[0] < open[0] && (open[0]-close[0]) >= bodyFraction * (high[0]-low[0]) && close[0] < lowest(low, lookback) over bars 1..lookback
candidates.book_order_type: market / limit at the close of the trend bar, scaling in higher

complexity.reason: lowest-low window plus a single-bar test

notes: Only in a channel with two-sided trading (T15-11, T15-27, T15-29); in a tight channel this is exactly where Brooks says not to fade.

candidates.name: StopBelowRecentSwingLow
candidates.quote: Other traders just buy with limit orders at one to three ticks below the low of the prior bar in a channel, risking to below the most recent swing low.
candidates.description: Protective stop for channel longs: exit when the close falls below the most recent swing low that existed at entry (proxy: lowest(low, stopLookback) captured at entry) minus stopTicks.
candidates.pseudocode: ctx.MarketPosition() > 0 && close[0] < swingLowAtEntry - stopTicks * tickSize
candidates.book_order_type: sell stop one tick below the swing low

complexity.reason: with the lowest-low proxy it is a value captured at entry; with true pivots it is hard

candidates.name: TwoBarReversalEntryBeyondBothBars
candidates.quote: The problem with entering below the low of the bar 7 bear bar is that the market often has a one-tick bear trap. ... This risk is less if you enter below the low of both bars
candidates.description: Two-bar reversal entry. Long side: bar[2] is a bear trend bar, bar[1] is a bull trend bar (the two-bar reversal), and bar[0] closes above the higher of the two bars' highs; buy at the next open. Entering beyond the extreme of both bars avoids the one-tick trap.
candidates.pseudocode: close[2] < open[2] && close[1] > open[1] && (close[1]-open[1]) >= bodyFraction * (high[1]-low[1]) && close[0] > max(high[1], high[2])
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the higher of the two bars

complexity.reason: three fixed-offset bars

notes: p276: scalpers' profit target five ticks beyond the signal bar low usually requires a six-tick move (T15-49).

candidates.name: ScalpProfitTargetTicks
candidates.quote: They exited with a one-point profit as bar 6 fell five ticks below the high of bar 4.
candidates.description: Scalp exit: open profit in price reaches scalpTicks x tick size (Emini scalp = 4 ticks / one point). Denominated in ticks, not dollars.
candidates.pseudocode: ctx.MarketPosition() > 0 && close[0] - ctx.EntryPrice() >= scalpTicks * tickSize
candidates.book_order_type: limit order at the scalp target

complexity.reason: entry price arithmetic

notes: Existing TakeProfit is in dollars; a tick/point version is a different parameterization and also serves T15-25's tick sizes.

candidates.name: ExitAtBreakevenAfterAdverseExcursion
candidates.quote: They could have bought back both shorts at the original entry price as the market fell to bar 31. Their original short would have broken even and their add-on would have made a one-point profit.
candidates.description: Breakeven exit for a scaled-in position: once the open loss has exceeded adverseTicks at some point, exit when price returns to the first entry price. Without pyramiding this reduces to 'exit at breakeven after an adverse excursion of X ticks'.
candidates.pseudocode: ctx.MarketPosition() > 0 && maxAdverseExcursionTicks >= adverseTicks && close[0] >= ctx.EntryPrice()
candidates.book_order_type: limit order at the first entry price

complexity.reason: needs the position's maximum adverse excursion persisted

notes: The engine's single-entry model cannot express the add-on profit; only the breakeven leg survives.

candidates.name: ConsecutiveTrendBarsSpike
candidates.quote: the market had eight consecutive bull trend bars in the strong bull spike up to bar 3, so the market was likely to have a test of the high after a pullback.
candidates.description: Spike filter: at least spikeBars consecutive bull trend bars ending at bar 0 (or ending within recentBars). Sets the expectation of a test of the spike high after a pullback (buy the pullback: T15-18, T15-25) and, per p270, marks climactic behaviour.
candidates.pseudocode: for all i in 0..spikeBars-1: close[i] > open[i] && (close[i]-open[i]) >= bodyFraction * (high[i]-low[i])
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (context)

complexity.reason: window loop

notes: ConsecutiveUpBars tests close > open only; the body-fraction test is the addition.
p266: every spike is a climax; consecutive climaxes lead to a larger correction (T15-57).

candidates.name: ConsecutiveBearBarsBlockFirstBuy
candidates.quote: Bar 4 was the fourth consecutive down bar, which is enough bearish momentum to make traders hesitant to buy above its high
candidates.description: Filter: do not buy the first reversal attempt when the pullback has had at least minBearBars consecutive bear bars; wait for a two-legged pullback (a high 2, T15-19).
candidates.pseudocode: count of consecutive bars ending at bar 1 with close < open < minBearBars
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (filter)

complexity.reason: short fixed-length loop

notes: p276 adds the fade: shorting on a limit at the high of that fourth bar was a reasonable scalp, which is T15-18 mirrored.

candidates.name: TrendingHighsLowsCloses
candidates.quote: The bulls would have looked at the rally up to bar 29 as having trending highs, lows, and closes, and therefore would have believed that it was strong.
candidates.description: Strength filter: each of the last windowBars has a higher high, higher low and higher close than the bar before it. When true, buying the breakout above the prior swing high on a stop is justified (p277).
candidates.pseudocode: for all i in 0..windowBars-1: high[i] > high[i+1] && low[i] > low[i+1] && close[i] > close[i+1]
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (context); the trade is a buy stop above the prior swing high

complexity.reason: window loop

candidates.name: FailedBreakoutBeyondPriorSwingHigh
candidates.quote: Since channels have two-sided trading, as long as the channel is not too tight and too steep, bears will short at or above swing highs.
candidates.description: Fade of a swing-point breakout in a two-sided channel. Long side (bear channel): the bar's low breaks below the lowest low of the prior lookback bars and the bar closes back above that level; buy at the next open.
candidates.pseudocode: lvl = lowest(low, lookback) over bars 1..lookback; low[0] < lvl && close[0] > lvl
candidates.book_order_type: limit at or one tick beyond the swing point, adding one point further

complexity.reason: lowest-low window

notes: p277: 'the high of bar 13 was exactly five ticks above bar 7' - bears added one point above the swing high.
Chapter 17 restates this for horizontal swing points; a pivot-based version is there (T17).

candidates.name: LastBreakoutTradeWonFilter
candidates.quote: Whenever a breakout trade results in a profit, it is a sign that the trend is strong.
candidates.description: Trend-strength filter from trade history: the most recently closed position was a with-trend breakout entry and it closed profitably. When true, favour further with-trend entries.
candidates.pseudocode: lastClosedTradeProfit > 0 && lastClosedTradeWasBreakout
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (filter)

complexity.reason: position-history read

notes: Needs the entry rule to tag itself as a breakout; the authoring pass may simplify to 'last trade won'.

candidates.name: CountertrendChannelIsFlag
candidates.quote: When a bull channel forms in a bear trend, it is a bear flag, and traders should look to short near the top, or on the pullback from a downside breakout.
candidates.description: A channel against the larger trend is a flag. Long side: a bear channel (two lower swing highs with comparable legs) forming while the larger trend is up (close above a slow EMA / close above close[trendLookback]); buy near the bottom of the bear channel (T15-15 mirrored) or the pullback after the upside breakout (T15-38).
candidates.pseudocode: BearChannelConfirmed && close[0] > ema(close, slowMaLength) && (ChannelLineOvershootReversal(long) || BreakoutPullbackEntry(long))
candidates.book_order_type: stop entries at the channel line reversal or breakout pullback

complexity.reason: channel detection plus a larger-trend context

notes: p257: even without a preceding trend every bull channel should be traded as a bear flag.

candidates.name: ConsecutiveClimaxCount
candidates.quote: This was the third or fourth consecutive buy climax (every spike, whether it is one bar or many bars, is a climax) ... Consecutive climaxes usually lead to a larger correction
candidates.description: Filter: the number of separate bull spikes (runs of >= spikeBars consecutive bull trend bars, separated by at least one non-spike bar) within the last windowBars is at least minClimaxes. When true, expect a larger correction: block new longs / allow fades.
candidates.pseudocode: count of disjoint runs of >= spikeBars bull trend bars within bars 0..windowBars-1 >= minClimaxes
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (context)

complexity.reason: run detection over a window with state

notes: Shown on a weekly SPY chart (Figure 15.4).

candidates.name: SpikeMeasuredMoveTarget
candidates.quote: Measured moves using the open or low of the first bar of the spike and the close or high of the last bar often are good areas for the bulls to take partial or full profits
candidates.description: Profit target after a spike of >= spikeBars consecutive bull trend bars: exit when high[0] >= spikeHigh + multiple x (spikeHigh - spikeOpen), where spikeOpen is the open of the first spike bar and spikeHigh the high of the last.
candidates.pseudocode: ctx.MarketPosition() > 0 && high[0] >= spikeHigh + multiple * (spikeHigh - spikeOpen)
candidates.book_order_type: limit order at the measured move

complexity.reason: spike run detection plus two persisted prices

notes: p250 (no-space page): a broader channel after a tight channel may reach a measured move based on the height of the tight channel - the same target with the tight channel as the spike.

candidates.name: MovingAverageGapBar
candidates.quote: Bar 7 was a second-entry moving average gap bar short in a bear trend, which often leads to the final leg in the bear trend before a larger reversal develops.
candidates.description: Long side: in a bull trend (close above EMA for most of the last trendBars), a bar forms entirely below the EMA (high[0] < ma): a moving average gap bar. Buy when the next bar closes above that bar's high. Brooks prefers the second entry.
candidates.pseudocode: high[1] < ma[1] && close[0] > high[1] && countBarsAboveMa(trendBars) >= trendBars * trendFraction
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop above the gap bar (second entry preferred)

complexity.reason: EMA plus a window count

notes: The full '20 gap bars' setup (a run of 20 bars not touching the EMA) is defined in the chapter 16/17 files.

candidates.name: IIPattern
candidates.quote: They could have shorted below the ii pattern at bar 18, or on any of the several following bars, as the market became always-in short.
candidates.description: Primitive: two consecutive inside bars (bar[1] inside bar[2], bar[0] inside bar[1]). The entry is a stop beyond the second inside bar; close-based: the next bar closes above high[0] of the ii (long) / below its low (short).
candidates.pseudocode: high[1] < high[2] && low[1] > low[2] && high[0] < high[1] && low[0] > low[1]
candidates.book_order_type: stop one tick beyond the ii

complexity.reason: three fixed-offset bars

notes: InsideBar covers one inside bar; ii is two. The direction is taken from the breakout, which makes the pattern itself direction-agnostic.

candidates.name: LowerHighAfterSelloffShortSetup
candidates.quote: even then it is often better not to short below a bar until after a sell-off that is then followed by a lower high.
candidates.description: Countertrend entry only after structure changes. Long side (fading a bear channel): a rally of >= ralliesBars bull bars, then a pullback that forms a higher swing low, then a bar closes above the prior bar's high; buy at the next open.
candidates.pseudocode: rally = at least rallyBars consecutive bull bars within the last windowBars; swingLow(1).price > swingLow(2).price formed after the rally; close[0] > high[1]
candidates.book_order_type: stop beyond the signal bar at the lower high

complexity.reason: needs a swing pivot formed after a detected spike

candidates.name: FirstHourExtremeFilter
candidates.quote: since the high or low of the day usually forms in the first hour and this was a possible high of the day.
candidates.description: Intraday context: after the first hour, if the session high was set during the first firstHourBars bars and price is now near it, treat the level as a possible high of day and favour low 2 shorts there (long side mirrored: possible low of day).
candidates.pseudocode: barsSinceSessionOpen > firstHourBars && sessionLowBarIndex < firstHourBars && close[0] <= sessionLow + nearAtr * atr(atrLength)
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (context)

complexity.reason: session-reset high/low tracking

candidates.name: PullbackStaysAboveMovingAverageForLongs
candidates.quote: There was a bear channel and the market was spending most of the day below the moving average.
candidates.description: Trend-side filter: the fraction of the last windowBars closing above the EMA is at least minFraction; when true trade the long side only (mirror for shorts).
candidates.pseudocode: count over i in 0..windowBars-1 of (close[i] > ma[i]) >= minFraction * windowBars
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (context)

complexity.reason: EMA plus a window count

notes: A cheap proxy for the always-in direction (T15-09).

chapter_summary: Chapter 15 defines channels as sloping trading ranges bounded by a trend line through two swing lows and a parallel channel line, and describes how to trade them: buy at the trend line and below prior bars' lows while always-in long, take profits at the channel line, fade overshoots only after three pushes, expect the first breakout of a tight channel to fail and successful breakouts to reach a measured move equal to the channel height. It produced the pivot/trend-line/channel-line primitive family (all hard), a set of simple window filters for channel character (tightness, slope, bar overlap, bear-body and tail counts, trending highs/lows/closes), several trivial fixed-offset bar patterns (breakout-vs-reversal bar strength, two-bar reversal, ii), and measured-move / channel-line / breakeven exits. Most of the chapter's second half is chart discussion that restates the same rules.
